raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #42919 ("[Model Loader] Let InstantTensor load DeepSeek-V4.1 with the Engram host table"): this branch carries its commit, and the diff to review is the last commit, "[DeepSeek-V4.1] Fill host-resident Engram rows with parallel positioned reads". #40453 (InstantTensor loader by YitaoYuan) is now on main. I will rebase this PR when #42919 lands.

## Motivation

With `--engram-config '{"placement": "cpu"}'`, the two Engram tables (188.8 GiB of rows and scales) live in pinned host memory, and each TP rank loads only its own row range. With one shard per rank (`"replication": "none"`), a rank holds 47.2 GiB at TP4. Under `--load-format instanttensor`, #42919 loads these files through the CPU safetensors iterator. That iterator returns memory-mapped tensors, so `EngramEmbedding._load_rows` copies its rows out of the file mapping one page fault at a time. On the setup below, that phase took 68.3 s (2.8 GiB/s aggregate over 4 ranks). This was more than half of the target model's load time.

A rank's rows are one contiguous byte range of the file. Large parallel reads straight into the pinned shard are much faster.

## Modifications

- `weight_utils.SafetensorsRowSource(path, offset, shape, dtype)`: a row-major checkpoint tensor that can be read by row range. `read_rows_into(dst, row_start)` checks the destination: contiguous CPU tensor, same dtype and row shape, range in bounds. It then fills `dst` with parallel `os.preadv` calls (8 threads, 64 MiB chunks) at the right file offsets, retrying short reads; a premature end of file raises. With `drop_page_cache=True`, it calls `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` after each chunk where available, so the kernel can drop the cached copy. That call is advisory, and its errors are logged at debug level.
- `weight_utils.host_resident_weights_iterator(files, patterns)`: reads offsets from the safetensors header. It yields a `SafetensorsRowSource` for tensor names that match the model's `host_resident_weight_patterns`, and memory-mapped tensors from `safe_open` for all other names.
- Under `--load-format instanttensor`, files with host-resident tensors now use this iterator. The `Source.host_resident_weight_patterns` docstring states that the matching parameters' weight loaders must accept a row source. `--weight-loader-disable-mmap` is not applied to these files: the tables are read with `preadv`, and the few other tensors in the files come from `safe_open`. With that flag, the previous path could not load these files: `safetensors.torch.load` (safetensors 0.8.0) has no `F8_E8M0` dtype.
- `EngramEmbedding._load_rows` reads only its own rows from a row source into the same destination as before: the rank's slice of the full table in the `shared` layout, or its whole shard in the `per_rank` layout. It requests page-cache eviction only in the `per_rank` layout, where this was measured; the `shared` layout keeps the page cache as before. Tensor inputs keep the existing copy. Row sources are only produced for host tables, so device tables are unchanged. The DSpark draft drops Engram names before it touches the value, so it reads no Engram rows.

## Accuracy Tests

Load-path change only; the rows loaded are byte-identical. New `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_host_resident_rows.py` (CPU) uses a checkpoint with an FP8 E4M3 table, its E8M0 scales, and an FP32 table:

- Random row ranges read through `read_rows_into` match the memory-mapped tensor byte for byte. Small chunks (1-77 bytes) and 1/3/8 threads exercise chunk boundaries inside rows and inside elements.
- A real `EngramEmbedding` is built for every rank at TP 1-4, with 37 rows (uneven splits). The `per_rank` and `shared` host layouts use a plain CPU buffer in place of the pinned host table, so the weight and scale are views into one buffer. The tensor path with CPU parameters is covered too. Loading from row sources gives the same bytes as loading from the memory-mapped tensors. In the `shared` layout, other ranks' rows are left untouched.
- Short reads are retried, a failing `posix_fadvise` does not fail the load, and a truncated file raises `EOFError`.
- `EngramEmbedding` requests page-cache eviction in the `per_rank` layout only, not in `shared` or for device tables.
- Destinations with a different dtype of the same size, a different row shape, an out-of-range row range, or non-contiguous memory are rejected.
- In `test_instanttensor_loader.py`, the host-resident names arrive as row sources with the full contents.

On this branch (current main plus #40453 and #42919), both files pass (21 tests) on macOS (CPU) and on Linux aarch64 (CPU, PyTorch 2.14.1); the Linux run covers the real `posix_fadvise` path. The rest of `test/registered/unit/model_loader/` also passes on macOS (139 passed, 1 skipped in total; `test_modelopt_loader.py` was not collected locally because `tvm_ffi` is not installed). Mutating the read offset, the chunk ranges, the short-read retry, the rank's `row_start`, or the dtype check makes the new tests fail.

Earlier, on an older main with the same production diff, a separate check used the real InstantTensor library on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU. Rows read into pinned buffers for every rank at TP 1-4 matched the memory map byte for byte and copied to the GPU unchanged. Pinned, `cudaHostRegister`ed host tables were exercised by the serving runs below.

#42787 (column-aligned Engram shards) changes how `row_start` and `rows` are chosen; `_load_rows` only consumes them, and the two branches merge without conflicts.

2026-10-29: rebased onto main `974831643f`, where #40453 and #42787 have landed (the branch now carries only the commit of #42919 and this one) and #46893 replaced the host-table variables with `--engram-config`, so the `per_rank` layout is now `"placement": "cpu"` with `"replication": "none"` (where page-cache eviction applies) and `shared` is `"replication": "per_node"`; the row test selects them through `--engram-config` and covers both the column-aligned and the equal-row split, both test files pass on the new head (21 tests, macOS CPU), and the SM120 GPU results in this description are from the previous head and will be re-run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4/EP4, 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, PCIe), DSpark draft, host Engram table (per-rank layout), checkpoint on local NVMe (ZFS), on an older main with the same production diff. A/B of this change on the same build, one server start each, timed from the server log. The "Engram files" time runs from the end of the InstantTensor stream to the Engram host-table completion message on TP0:

| | Engram files (188.8 GiB) | Target model load (TP0) | Process start to ready |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (#42919) | 68.3 s (2.8 GiB/s) | 119.9 s | 3 m 43 s |
| this PR | 13.5 s (14.0 GiB/s) | 64.0 s | 2 m 46 s |

For reference, the default safetensors loader takes 264.2 s for the target model on the same setup. The time spent on the device files (about 40 s) and the DSpark draft load (40.0 s before, 39.5 s after) did not change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+def _split_host_resident_files(
+    files: List[str], patterns: Optional[Tuple[str, ...]]
+) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]:
+    """Split safetensors files into (device, host) groups, keeping their order.
+
+    A file goes to the host group when any tensor name in its header contains
+    one of ``patterns``. Only headers are read.
+    """
+    if not patterns:
+        return list(files), []
+    from safetensors.torch import safe_open
+
+    device_files, host_files = [], []
+    for path in files:
+        host = False
+        # Other files stay in the device group; InstantTensor rejects them.
+        if path.endswith(".safetensors"):
+            with safe_open(path, framework="pt") as f:
+                host = any(p in name for name in f.keys() for p in patterns)
+        (host_files if host else device_files).append(path)
+    return device_files, host_files
+
+
+def _to_device_unless_host_resident(
+    weights: Iterable[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]], patterns: Tuple[str, ...]
+) -> Generator[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor], None, None]:
+    """Move tensors that are not host-resident to the current device, where
+    InstantTensor puts every other tensor, so tensors that are combined
+    during loading share a device."""
+    for name, tensor in weights:
+        if not any(p in name for p in patterns):
+            tensor = tensor.to(current_platform.get_device(torch.cuda.current_device()))
+        yield name, tensor
+

 import itertools
 import json
 import logging
+import math
 import os
 import re
 import struct
@@ -1192,6 +1193,100 @@ def get_pp_stage_load_group() -> LoadGroup:
     return parallel.tp_group if parallel.pp_size > 1 else _DEFAULT_LOAD_GROUP
 
 
+class SafetensorsRowSource:
+    """A row-major safetensors tensor that is read by row range on demand.
+
+    A rank's rows are one contiguous byte range of the file, so a row-sharded
+    host-resident weight can fill its own destination with positioned reads
+    instead of copying out of a memory map page by page.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, path: str, offset: int, shape: Tuple[int, ...], dtype: torch.dtype
+    ):
+        self.path = path
+        self.offset = offset
+        self.shape = tuple(shape)
+        self.dtype = dtype
+        self.row_bytes = math.prod(self.shape[1:]) * dtype.itemsize
+
+    def read_rows_into(
+        self,
+        dst: torch.Tensor,
+        row_start: int,
+        drop_page_cache: bool = False,
+        num_threads: int = 8,
+        chunk_bytes: int = 64 << 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Read rows ``[row_start, row_start + len(dst))`` into ``dst``.
+
+        With ``drop_page_cache``, ask the kernel to evict each range once read.
+        """
+        rows = dst.shape[0]
+        if dst.device.type != "cpu" or not dst.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("SafetensorsRowSource reads into contiguous CPU tensors")
+        if (
+            dst.dtype != self.dtype
+            or tuple(dst.shape[1:]) != self.shape[1:]
+            or row_start < 0
+            or row_start + rows > self.shape[0]
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"rows {row_start}:{row_start + rows} of {self.dtype} {self.shape} "
+                f"do not fit {dst.dtype} {tuple(dst.shape)}"
+            )
+        total = rows * self.row_bytes
+        if total == 0:
+            return
+        view = memoryview(dst.view(-1).view(torch.uint8).numpy())
+        base = self.offset + row_start * self.row_bytes
+        fd = os.open(self.path, os.O_RDONLY)
+        try:
+
+            def read(start: int) -> None:
+                end = min(start + chunk_bytes, total)
+                done = start
+                while done < end:
+                    n = os.preadv(fd, [view[done:end]], base + done)
+                    if n <= 0:
+                        raise EOFError(f"short read from {self.path} at {base + done}")
+                    done += n
+                # The bytes now live in dst; ask the kernel to drop the cached copy.
+                if drop_page_cache and hasattr(os, "posix_fadvise"):
+                    try:
+                        os.posix_fadvise(
+                            fd, base + start, end - start, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED
+                        )
+                    except OSError as e:
+                        logger.debug("posix_fadvise failed for %s: %s", self.path, e)
+
+            with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(num_threads) as pool:
+                list(pool.map(read, range(0, total, chunk_bytes)))
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+

+    hf_weights_files: List[str], patterns: Tuple[str, ...]

+                    tensor = SafetensorsRowSource(
+                        path, 8 + header_len + begin, tensor.shape, tensor.dtype
+                    )
+                yield name, tensor

+

+from sglang.srt.arg_groups.engram_config import (
+    EngramConfig,
+    EngramLookup,
+    EngramPlacement,
+    EngramReplication,
+)

+    SafetensorsRowSource,

+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase

+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+NUM_ROWS, DIM = 37, 64  # 37 rows split unevenly over 2, 3 and 4 ranks.
+# Hash-column segments of the table (prefix sums): 12 columns shard on column
+# boundaries over 1-4 ranks; 5 columns fall back to the equal-row split.
+COLUMN_BOUNDS = {
+    "columns": (0, 2, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 34, 37),
+    "rows": (0, 7, 14, 22, 29, 37),
+}
+WEIGHT = "layers.1.engram.embed.weight"
+SCALE = "layers.1.engram.embed.scale"
+FP32_TABLE = "layers.1.engram.embed.fp32"
+OTHER = "layers.1.engram.wkv.weight"
+HOST_RESIDENT = (WEIGHT, SCALE, FP32_TABLE)
+SENTINEL = 0xA5
+# --engram-config per layout: device shards, a host shard per rank, or one host
+# table per node. An explicit lookup skips the auto choice, which probes GPUs.
+LAYOUTS = {
+    None: EngramConfig(lookup=EngramLookup.ALL_REDUCE),
+    "per_rank": EngramConfig(
+        placement=EngramPlacement.CPU, lookup=EngramLookup.ALL_REDUCE
+    ),
+    "shared": EngramConfig(
+        placement=EngramPlacement.CPU,
+        replication=EngramReplication.PER_NODE,
+        lookup=EngramLookup.ALL_REDUCE,
+    ),
+}
+
+
+class _FakeHostTable:
+    """_HostTable without the memfd, the huge pages and cudaHostRegister."""
+
+    def __init__(self, replication, nbytes, name, group):
+        self.replication = replication
+        self.dirty = False
+        self.bytes = torch.full((nbytes,), SENTINEL, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        self.device_ptr = self.bytes.data_ptr()
+
+
+def _random_bytes(shape, dtype, generator):
+    raw = torch.randint(0, 256, shape, dtype=torch.uint8, generator=generator)
+    return raw.view(dtype)
+
+
+class TestHostResidentRows(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
+        self.path = os.path.join(folder.name, "model-00002.safetensors")
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+        self.tensors = {
+            WEIGHT: _random_bytes((NUM_ROWS, DIM), torch.float8_e4m3fn, g),
+            SCALE: _random_bytes(
+                (NUM_ROWS, DIM // engram.FP8_BLOCK_SIZE), torch.float8_e8m0fnu, g
+            ),
+            # Multi-byte elements, so small chunks split elements across reads.
+            FP32_TABLE: torch.randn(NUM_ROWS, 5, generator=g),
+            OTHER: torch.randn(8, 16, generator=g),
+        }
+        save_file(self.tensors, self.path)
+        self.items = dict(host_resident_weights_iterator([self.path], (".embed.",)))
+        with safe_open(self.path, framework="pt") as f:
+            self.mmap = {name: f.get_tensor(name) for name in self.tensors}
+
+    def assertBytesEqual(self, actual, expected, msg=None):
+        self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, expected.dtype, msg)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8)), msg
+        )
+
+    def test_iterator_yields_row_sources_for_matching_names(self):
+        self.assertCountEqual(self.items, self.tensors)
+        for name in HOST_RESIDENT:
+            source = self.items[name]
+            self.assertIsInstance(source, SafetensorsRowSource)
+            self.assertEqual(source.shape, tuple(self.tensors[name].shape))
+            self.assertEqual(source.dtype, self.tensors[name].dtype)
+        self.assertBytesEqual(self.items[OTHER], self.tensors[OTHER])
+
+    def test_random_row_ranges_match_mmap(self):
+        rng = random.Random(0)
+        for name in HOST_RESIDENT:
+            full = self.mmap[name]
+            for _ in range(30):
+                start = rng.randrange(NUM_ROWS + 1)
+                rows = rng.randrange(NUM_ROWS - start + 1)
+                chunk_bytes = rng.choice([1, 3, 8, 77, 1 << 20])
+                num_threads = rng.choice([1, 3, 8])
+                dst = torch.empty((rows, *full.shape[1:]), dtype=full.dtype)
+                self.items[name].read_rows_into(
+                    dst, start, num_threads=num_threads, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes
+                )
+                self.assertBytesEqual(
+                    dst,
+                    full[start : start + rows],
+                    f"{name} rows {start}:{start + rows}, chunk {chunk_bytes}",
+                )
+
+    def test_short_reads_and_failed_cache_advice(self):
+        real_preadv = os.preadv
+
+        def short_preadv(fd, buffers, offset):
+            return real_preadv(fd, [buffers[0][:5]], offset)
+
+        def failing_fadvise(*_args):
+            raise OSError(errno.ENOSYS, "posix_fadvise")
+
+        dst = torch.empty(10, 5)
+        with (
+            patch.object(weight_utils.os, "preadv", short_preadv),
+            patch.object(
+                weight_utils.os, "posix_fadvise", failing_fadvise, create=True
+            ),
+            patch.object(weight_utils.os, "POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED", 4, create=True),
+        ):
+            self.items[FP32_TABLE].read_rows_into(
+                dst, 3, drop_page_cache=True, num_threads=3, chunk_bytes=64
+            )
+        self.assertBytesEqual(dst, self.mmap[FP32_TABLE][3:13])
+
+    def test_page_cache_eviction_only_for_per_rank_tables(self):
+        for layout, expected in ((None, False), ("per_rank", True), ("shared", False)):
+            calls = []
+            with (
+                patch.object(
+                    weight_utils.os,
+                    "posix_fadvise",
+                    lambda *args: calls.append(args),
+                    create=True,
+                ),
+                patch.object(weight_utils.os, "POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED", 4, create=True),
+            ):
+                self._load_engram(2, 1, layout, self.items)
+            self.assertEqual(bool(calls), expected, layout)
+
+    def test_truncated_file_raises(self):
+        path = self.path + ".copy"
+        shutil.copyfile(self.path, path)
+        source = dict(host_resident_weights_iterator([path], (".embed.",)))[WEIGHT]
+        os.truncate(path, source.offset + 2 * source.row_bytes)
+
+        dst = torch.empty(2, DIM, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        source.read_rows_into(dst, 0)
+        self.assertBytesEqual(dst, self.tensors[WEIGHT][:2])
+        with self.assertRaises(EOFError):
+            source.read_rows_into(torch.empty_like(dst), 1)
+
+    def _load_engram(self, tp_size, tp_rank, layout, weights, split="columns"):
+        """Load WEIGHT and SCALE into one rank's EngramEmbedding."""
+        parallel = SimpleNamespace(tp_size=tp_size, tp_rank=tp_rank, tp_group=None)
+        with (
+            patch.object(engram, "get_parallel", return_value=parallel),
+            patch.object(engram, "_HostTable", _FakeHostTable),
+            patch.object(engram, "_sorted_host_reads", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(engram.torch.cuda, "current_device", return_value=0),
+            get_context().override_server_args(),
+            get_exec().offload.override(engram_config=LAYOUTS[layout]),
+        ):
+            embed = engram.EngramEmbedding(
+                NUM_ROWS, DIM, layer_id=1, column_bounds=COLUMN_BOUNDS[split]
+            )
+        for param, name in ((embed.weight, WEIGHT), (embed.scale, SCALE)):
+            param.weight_loader(param, weights[name])
+        return embed
+
+    def test_engram_shards_match_mmap_path(self):
+        # Device rows, and both host-table layouts with weight and scale
+        # carved out of one host buffer.
+        for layout, split, tp_size in itertools.product(
+            (None, "per_rank", "shared"), COLUMN_BOUNDS, (1, 2, 3, 4)
+        ):
+            for tp_rank in range(tp_size):
+                msg = f"{layout=} {split=} {tp_size=} {tp_rank=}"
+                via_mmap = self._load_engram(tp_size, tp_rank, layout, self.mmap, split)
+                via_rows = self._load_engram(
+                    tp_size, tp_rank, layout, self.items, split
+                )
+                rows = slice(via_rows.row_start, via_rows.row_start + via_rows.rows)
+                for name in ("weight", "scale"):
+                    actual = getattr(via_rows, name).data
+                    self.assertBytesEqual(actual, getattr(via_mmap, name).data, msg)
+                    own = actual[rows] if layout == "shared" else actual
+                    expected = self.tensors[WEIGHT if name == "weight" else SCALE]
+                    self.assertBytesEqual(own, expected[rows], msg)
+                    if layout == "shared":
+                        # Other ranks' rows are left untouched.
+                        others = torch.ones(NUM_ROWS, dtype=torch.bool)
+                        others[rows] = False
+                        untouched = actual[others].view(torch.uint8) == SENTINEL
+                        self.assertTrue(untouched.all(), msg)
+                if layout is not None:
+                    self.assertTrue(via_rows.host_table.dirty, msg)
+
+    def test_rejects_mismatched_destinations(self):
+        source = self.items[WEIGHT]
+        for dst, row_start in (
+            (torch.empty(3, DIM, dtype=torch.float8_e5m2), 0),  # same size, wrong dtype
+            (torch.empty(3, DIM - 1, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn), 0),
+            (torch.empty(4, DIM, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn), NUM_ROWS - 3),
+            (torch.empty(DIM, 3, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn).t(), 0),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(shape=tuple(dst.shape), row_start=row_start):
+                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                    source.read_rows_into(dst, row_start)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
